method: ENTIRELY from AMH across three pages, read under subscription and PARAPHRASED: no passage reproduced, no source_text stored, every claim carries its page's locator and the verdict licensed_source_not_quoted, so NOTHING here is machine re-checkable. A targeted search of RACGP's open AJGP found no current Australian article on cutaneous or anogenital warts; that absence is recorded rather than filled with an older or overseas source. Salicylic acid is named by AMH as the treatment of choice for cutaneous warts and ITS MONOGRAPH WAS NOT RETRIEVED, so the first-line treatment in this guideline carries no strength, frequency or duration -- which is stated plainly rather than filled from memory.

claims.claim: Warts are caused by human papillomavirus with different genotypes infecting particular locations, and are classified by location and morphology as cutaneous warts including common, flat, mosaic, plantar and palmar warts, anogenital warts, and other warts including oral, laryngeal, conjunctival and nasal warts
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states specialist referral is required if warts are large, extensive or in certain locations such as urethral, intra-anal or cervical, for pregnant women with anogenital warts, if the diagnosis is in doubt, or if standard treatments fail
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states that in immunocompetent individuals cutaneous warts may disappear without treatment within a few months or years, and that treatment should be considered when warts are a cosmetic problem or cause unwanted effects such as pain, functional impairment or psychological distress
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Choice of treatment for cutaneous warts depends on factors such as location and number of warts, previous treatments, and patient preference
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states salicylic acid is the treatment of choice for cutaneous warts as it is relatively safe, inexpensive and may be used at home, that it is irritant and not suitable for application to the face or broken skin with frequency reduced if discomfort occurs, and that if warts remain after 3 months of treatment cryotherapy should be considered
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states that for cutaneous warts other treatments are preferred over podophyllum resin as evidence of efficacy is lacking and close supervision is required due to risk of systemic toxicity, and that its use is contraindicated in pregnancy
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states some anogenital warts may disappear without treatment within a year, and that treatment should be considered when warts cause unwanted effects such as itch, pain, bleeding or psychological distress
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states imiquimod is first line for self-treatment of external anogenital warts, that it works by modifying the immune response and has the advantage of less frequent application, and that other treatments are preferred in pregnancy
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states podophyllotoxin, available via the Special Access Scheme, is second line for self-treatment of external anogenital warts, that it is irritant but has low systemic toxicity, and that its use is contraindicated in pregnancy
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states trichloroacetic acid has been used by some specialists to treat internal and external anogenital warts, that it is highly irritant and not suitable for self-treatment, and that it is mainly used in pregnancy
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states cryotherapy usually with liquid nitrogen may be used for both cutaneous and anogenital warts, that it requires multiple treatments, is painful essentially preventing use in young children, and may cause scarring, dyspigmentation, infection and rarely damage to underlying nerves
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states electrosurgery, excision or laser are further options depending on location, and that some specialists may consider these methods when topical agents or cryotherapy fail or are not suitable
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states that human papillomavirus may persist after treatment and recurrence is common
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH advises removing any excess skin from cutaneous warts with a blade, pumice stone or emery board before applying treatment, treating plantar warts at pressure points with non-surgical methods to reduce the risk of painful scarring, and considering referral to a podiatrist
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH advises telling patients with cutaneous warts about ways to reduce spreading the infection such as avoiding skin maceration or trauma to warts and wearing thongs in public showers and change rooms
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states that as human papillomavirus may persist after treatment it can be transmitted even when no warts are visible, and that using a condom may reduce the risk of transmission
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states that HPV vaccination protects against the HPV types that commonly cause anogenital warts, reducing their incidence
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, therapeutic topic 'Warts' (Dermatological drugs > Drugs for warts) at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/warts, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Imiquimod enhances the immune response to viral infections and tumours by inducing immune system cells as well as interferon and other cytokines, and is indicated for external genital and perianal warts, superficial basal cell carcinoma where surgery is inappropriate, and actinic keratoses of the face and scalp
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Imiquimod' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/imiquimod, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH gives the imiquimod dose for external genital and perianal warts in adults and children as applied to the affected area 3 times a week, for example Monday, Wednesday and Friday, left on for 6 to 10 hours, continued until total clearance of warts or for a maximum of 16 weeks, and notes the median time to total wart clearance is 10 weeks
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Imiquimod' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/imiquimod, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states imiquimod efficacy may be reduced in HIV and immunocompromised patients, that there is a theoretical risk of reduced immunosuppressant activity with immunosuppressants, that autoimmune and inflammatory skin disorders such as psoriasis and eczema may be exacerbated, and that broken skin raises the potential for increased systemic absorption
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Imiquimod' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/imiquimod, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states imiquimod commonly causes local skin reactions including erythema, itch, burning sensation, erosion, ulceration, blisters, exfoliation, skin hardening, oedema, scabbing and hypo- or hyperpigmentation which may be permanent, with rare severe skin reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and erythema multiforme
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Imiquimod' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/imiquimod, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH advises applying imiquimod before bedtime as a thin layer to the wart after washing and drying the area, washing it off with mild soap and water about 6 to 10 hours later, washing hands before and after use, and avoiding bathing or showering after application
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Imiquimod' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/imiquimod, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states that imiquimod cream may weaken condoms and diaphragms and should be washed off before they are used, and that if the patient decides to have sex the cream should be applied afterwards or washed off if already applied
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Imiquimod' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/imiquimod, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH states imiquimod is not approved for urethral, intravaginal, cervical, rectal or intra-anal warts

claims.claim: AMH states imiquimod has limited data in pregnancy and although it should be safe to use given minimal or poor absorption, other treatments for anogenital warts are preferred
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Imiquimod' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/imiquimod, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: Podophyllotoxin, also known as podofilox, is the major active constituent of podophyllum resin, binds to tubulin arresting mitosis in metaphase and leading to epithelial cell death, is indicated for external anogenital warts, and is not marketed in Australia though it may be available through the Special Access Scheme
claims.locator: AMH Medicines, drug monograph 'Podophyllotoxin' at https://amhonline.amh.net.au/chapters/dermatological-drugs/drugs-warts/podophyllotoxin, July 2026 release, read under subscription 2026-09-22

claims.claim: AMH gives the podophyllotoxin regimen for adults and children over 2 years as a 7-day treatment cycle applying the liquid twice a day for 3 days followed by no treatment for 4 days, with the cycle repeated as necessary for up to 4 or 5 cycles
